label: rem:phase-transition-interpretation
title: Three phases from Hecke channels and the triple point
html:
The Hecke algebra H_n(q) carries irreducible representations corresponding to Young diagrams. At a generic temperature T_q, a single representation dominates the partition function. At a critical temperature T_q^{(c)}, two representations contribute equally, introducing a non-analyticity into the partition function.

The three phases.

  1. Gas (symmetric channel, eigenvalue q). At high T_q, each knot confines to a single S^3 fibre. The equation of state mirrors the quantum ideal gas law.
  2. Liquid (mixed channel). At intermediate T_q, knots initiate Hopf-linking across fibres through the Hopf base S^2. This inter-fibre linking establishes structural correlations.
  3. Solid (antisymmetric channel, eigenvalue -q^{-1}). At low T_q, inter-fibre links dominate. Knots form a rigid braid lattice, occupying the strict sign representation.

Sublimation mechanism. The Hecke algebra supplies no mechanism. The three channels are complementary summands, not an extension of one by another: at a substrate parameter that is not a root of unity H_n(q) is semisimple, so every short exact sequence of H_n(q)-modules splits and no extension class distinguishes an unstable liquid phase from a stable one (prop:phase-transition-boundary). The correlation with odd crossing number recorded in rem:composite-crossing-sublimation-criteria stands on its own arithmetic and carries no derivation from here.

Triple point. All three phases coexist only when three Hecke representations contribute identically. This defines a rigid codimension-2 condition in the (T_q, P_q) plane. It obeys the Gibbs phase rule.

Classical theory comparison. Classical theory generates phase transitions artificially by appending ad hoc inter-particle potentials (van der Waals or Lennard-Jones) to the ideal gas. The QOU generates physical interactions through inter-fibre braid linking across the Hopf base of S^3_q. The S^3 topology supplies the binding potential via its boundary action. The Hecke representation theory dictates the exact discrete phase structure.
